edition.alertText: IRGC claims gas carrier exploded after mine strike in eastern Hormuz (Nov 13) — 3 vessels hit in single day; CENTCOM shoots down 2 IRGC drones targeting Bahrain, denies Iranian claim of US radar destroyed; IRGC launches 6 drones at US radar at Al-Riffa base in Bahrain (Nov 15) — Bahrain intercepts, first attacks since September; Bahrain condemns 'systematic hostile approach,' cites Article 51; IRGC claims supertanker with 2M+ bbl sank after mine strike (Nov 15); UKMTO: tanker attacked in Arabian Gulf near Hormuz — Indian shipping authorities report, crew safe; USS Theodore Roosevelt CSG enters CENTCOM AOR — 3rd carrier in theater; Trump told advisers he may hold off on Iran attacks if no new provocations (Reuters); Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral summit set for Nov 19 in Shenzhen — Iran on agenda; Rubio: 'no need for military action' — economic pressure sufficient; Saudi intercepts 2 Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh + 6 drones and 2 missiles at Mecca, Medina, Eastern Province; Houthi missile kills 5 near Aden; Yemeni government forces withdraw from Bab el-Mandeb positions — Houthis tighten grip on strait approaches; Houthis release 600 POWs (ICRC); G7 condemns Iran attacks and Houthi strikes; UN official warns 45 million face food insecurity — urges immediate fertilizer corridor through Hormuz; Ghalibaf: Iran ready for war or negotiations; Araghchi to visit Muscat Tuesday for Hormuz shipping talks; oil flat on week — Brent settles $95.84, WTI $88.56; gold nearly flat at ~$3,888; CENTCOM: 1.7B+ bbl exported under US protection; UKMTO: 163 conflict-related maritime incidents since war began; Mossad chief Gofman meets CIA director in Washington

situation: The diplomatic trajectory shifted over the weekend toward a holding pattern ahead of the landmark Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral summit in Shenzhen on November 19 — the first three-way meeting between US, Chinese, and Russian leaders. The White House confirmed that Iran will be on the agenda, while Ukraine will not be discussed. Trump signaled a pause in military escalation, telling senior advisers he may hold off on attacking Iran if Tehran and the Houthis refrain from new provocations, according to Reuters, which also reported that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Turkey's President Erdogan had both urged Trump not to resume strikes after the midterms. Secretary of State Rubio declared there was 'no need for military action' given the devastating economic pressure already inflicted on Iran's economy. However, Trump's earlier 'no deal' rhetoric from November 12 — when he reassigned Vance from Iran talks and declared the US doesn't need a deal — remains the operative policy framework, with the naval blockade continuing at full effect. Iran's Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf stated Tehran is ready for 'war or negotiations' and will not remain in a state of 'neither war nor peace,' while Foreign Minister Araghchi is scheduled to visit Muscat on Tuesday for talks with Oman's FM on restoring unhindered shipping through Hormuz. The Mossad chief met the CIA director in Washington on November 13, with reports suggesting Netanyahu is pressing for renewed action against Iran's nuclear program. The G7 issued a joint condemnation of Iranian attacks on neighboring countries and Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia, calling for an immediate halt to military operations.

Oil prices ended Friday's session essentially flat, closing out a second consecutive weekly decline as the supply surplus narrative competed with persistent attack risks. Brent settled at $95.84/bbl, up just 2 cents on the day but down approximately 2.5% for the week — its second straight weekly loss after the previous week's 16% plunge. WTI closed at $88.56/bbl, down 0.2% on the day. The weekly decline reflected growing expectations of a supply surplus, with rising US crude inventories (up 4.7 million barrels to 414.4 million, versus an expected 1.1 million draw) and softer demand weighing on prices despite unabated Hormuz attack claims. US stocks closed mixed on Friday — the Dow rose 0.1%, the S&P 500 fell 0.4%, and the Nasdaq dropped 0.9%. Gold steadied at approximately $3,888/oz, up a fraction on Friday after reaching a one-year low at $3,885 on Thursday, but still posted one of its worst weeks in four months as bets on further US rate hikes intensified. Silver fell 2.6% to $48.65/oz, hitting a one-year low. The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group entered CENTCOM's area of operations on Sunday, joining the George Washington and George H.W. Bush — marking the first time three US carriers are operating in the Arabian Sea theater simultaneously. CENTCOM reported that over 1.7 billion barrels of crude oil had moved through the Strait of Hormuz under US protection, up from 1.5 billion reported previously, with approximately 150 vessels diverted and five disabled under the blockade since July.

Iran continued its near-daily pattern of mine-strike claims throughout the weekend, while a significant escalation saw IRGC drones target a US base in Bahrain for the first time since September. On November 13, the IRGC claimed a gas carrier transporting LNG struck a mine and exploded in the eastern Strait of Hormuz on an 'unauthorized and dangerous' route, followed by Iranian navy and army claims of two additional tankers hitting mines the same day. On November 14, Iran's military reported fires on at least two more tankers from mine strikes, bringing the 24-hour claimed total to five vessels. By Sunday November 15, the IRGC claimed a supertanker carrying over two million barrels of oil sank after hitting a mine — none of these claims have been independently confirmed by CENTCOM or UKMTO. Also on November 13, the IRGC said it had destroyed a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for a strike on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, Hormozgan Province; CENTCOM denied any damage, saying it shot down both one-way attack drones. On November 15, the IRGC launched a more ambitious attack — six drones targeting a US radar installation at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain. Bahrain's Defence Force said it intercepted and destroyed all incoming aerial attacks. UKMTO reported a tanker attacked in the Arabian Gulf near Hormuz on Sunday, with Indian shipping authorities confirming the crew was safe. UKMTO has now logged 163 conflict-related maritime incidents since the war began on February 28, with eight during the November 8-15 reporting week. In Yemen, the Houthi front expanded dangerously: Saudi air defenses intercepted two ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, six drones and two more missiles targeting Mecca, Medina, and the Eastern Province on Saturday. A Houthi missile struck a checkpoint near Aden, killing five. Most significantly, Yemeni government forces withdrew from positions overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, including Dhubab Airport, ceding control of the approaches to the Houthis and reversing gains from an October offensive. The UN's Jorge Moreira da Silva, speaking at the COP31 summit in Antalya, warned that 45 million people could face severe food insecurity and urged the US and Iran to immediately allow fertilizer shipments through Hormuz, proposing about five vessels per day within 7-10 days.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne — more than doubled since pre-war — feeding into phosphate production costs; Egypt, Brazil, India cutting output. Mosaic phosphate plants remain curtailed including South Fort Meade (Florida) — 199 workers laid off. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%; DAP at $803/mt in October, ~30% above January (IFDC). Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst). China phosphate exports near zero in 2026, down from ~5.3M mt in 2025 (IFDC).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for fourth consecutive month — September, October, and early November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group/Fertilizer Daily). UN official Jorge Moreira da Silva at COP31 (Nov 14) warns 45 million people could face severe food insecurity — urges US and Iran to immediately allow ~5 fertilizer vessels/day through Hormuz within 7-10 days. Fertilizer prices up ~30% since blockades began (UN). Sudan food prices doubled in 6 months; Nepal farmers cannot afford fertiliser. Countries facing significant impact: Mozambique, Kenya, Sudan, Somalia, Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka. Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). DAP at $803/mt in October, urea near January levels after April spike (IFDC Bulletin #37). Egypt gas supply cuts to fertilizer producers rose from 20% to 33% on Nov 8 — AGF Nitrogen running at 80-85% capacity (IFDC). Russia export quotas Dec 2026–May 2027 at ~18.8M mt, down from ~20M mt. IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement. Middle East fertiliser exports declined by 70% as Iran war disrupts supplies (The National).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Qatar LNG loadings pick up to roughly half of pre-war levels (Bloomberg, Nov 10). Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas eased to ~€89.59/MWh (~$100.85), down from 4-year high above €101/MWh prior week; EU gas storage at 74.33% full vs 86% five-year average — lowest in over a decade entering winter (IEA). LNG crossings at Hormuz reached 32 in October — highest since war began (S&P Global). IRGC claims gas carrier exploded after mine strike in eastern Hormuz (Nov 13). Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs €2B higher amid Iran war. Europe and Asia face tight supply heading into winter. JERA CEO says Qatar LNG supply unlikely to recover soon. EIA projects US heating oil households to pay $2,977 this winter — up 70.2% from last year.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals

Allianz Trade estimates >$200B in physical damage across GCC — 80+ energy facilities struck, a third severely damaged; cumulative economic losses projected at $790B through 2030.
